plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their behavior. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid up or down. Bidding your true value of $3 ensures you win only when it's profitable (i.e., when the second-highest bid is below your value) and never overpay. I will bid exactly my value.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values. The dominant strategy in such auctions is to bid exactly my true value, as I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid. Bidding my value ($24) ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value exceeds the second-highest bid) and never overpay. Bidding higher risks winning at a loss; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.
